The 26th annual meeting of the APS Northwest Section was hosted by the [Oregon Institute of Technology](https://www.oit.edu) in Klamath Falls, Oregon. This page is the meeting website as it stood before the meeting, with registration, abstract submission, and travel grant links removed.

- [Program guide](program-guide.qmd)
- [Schedule and abstracts in the APS meeting archive](https://meetings-archive.aps.org/nws/2026/)

## Date and Location

The meeting was held **June 4–6, 2026** at the Oregon Institute of Technology in Klamath Falls, Oregon.

[Oregon Institute of Technology](https://www.oit.edu)
3201 Campus Dr
Klamath Falls, Oregon 97601

The banquet was held at the [Running Y Resort](https://runningy.com/) on Friday, June 5.

## Getting Here

### By Car

Klamath Falls is located in Southern Oregon at the intersection of OR-140 and US-97.

### By Plane

The nearest airport is in Medford, Oregon (MFR).
The airport is about 70 miles from Klamath Falls.

Rental cars are available at the airport.

There are also buses that run between Medford and downtown Klamath Falls each day. The bus stops at the Medford airport, the Running Y, and downtown Klamath Falls, and costs about $25 each way. You can [purchase tickets](https://www.oregon-point.com/tickets/southwest) through Greyhound, Amtrak, and other carriers, but it is all [the same route and carrier](https://www.oregon-point.com/routes/southwest).

Other airports in the region include

- Redmond, Oregon — RDM, about 120 miles (near Bend, Oregon)
- Redding, California — RDD, about 120 miles
- Reno/Tahoe, Nevada — RNO, about 250 miles
- Portland, Oregon — PDX, about 290 miles
- Sacramento, California — SMF, about 290 miles

### By Train

Amtrak's scenic [Coast Starlight](https://www.amtrak.com/routes/coast-starlight-train) train connects Los Angeles to Portland and Seattle, and passes through Klamath Falls twice a day (8 a.m. northbound, 10 p.m. southbound).

## Student Support

Travel support was available for students, with awards of up to $300 paid after the meeting to confirmed attendees.

We recognized outstanding student presentations at the meeting:

- **Best Student Poster** — first place and honorable mention
- **Best Student Talk** — first place and honorable mention

## Things to Do In and Around Klamath Falls

Klamath Falls has a pleasant and walkable downtown with several breweries and coffee roasters. You can explore Western art and Native American artifacts at the Favell Museum. Opportunities for hiking, kayaking, and mountain biking abound in the surrounding area, with nearby Moore Park offering lakefront trails and Cascade views. (Expect pleasant June weather with highs in the 70s–80s°F and cool evenings.)

You can also …

- Play golf at the [Running Y](https://runningy.com/) — Oregon's only Arnold Palmer-designed signature golf course
- Attend the [Oregon Shakespeare Festival](https://www.osfashland.org/) in Ashland, Oregon
- Visit [Crater Lake National Park](https://www.nps.gov/crla)
- Hike and spelunk at [Lava Beds National Monument](https://www.nps.gov/labe/)
- Watch for birds along the [Klamath Basin Birding Trail](https://www.klamathbirdingtrails.com/), at the [Lower Klamath National Wildlife Refuge](https://www.fws.gov/refuge/lower-klamath), or at the [Upper Klamath National Wildlife Refuge](https://www.fws.gov/refuge/upper-klamath) (all part of the Pacific Flyway)
